newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: FORECAST-Minister sees Kazakh GDP rising this year.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Minister sees Kazakh GDP rising this year.

text.p: Kazakhstan's economy will grow this year and next, ending several years of recession, Economy Minister Umirzak Shukeyev said on Thursday.
The government expects Kazakhstan's gross domestic product to rise 0.5 percent this year and another two percent in 1997, he told an investment conference. GDP fell by 8.9 percent last year.
Annual inflation was likely to slow this year to 30 percent from 60 percent last year, and will slow further to 17.5 percent in 1997.
Shukeyev said external debt accounted for only 20 percent of GDP, but did not give absolute figures.

The government plans to attract in the near future in the economy a total of $1.2 billion of investment, and Shukeyev said foreign investors could be tempted by the country's huge natural resorces estimated at $10.4 trillion.
"Kazakhstan's investment environment is favourable," he said.
In particular, the government is looking for $658 million to be invested in the power industry and another $1.8 billion for the transport sector.

Shukeyev said that Kazakhstan's air transport needed $275 million, including $260 million to build an international airport in the city of Akmola which has been designated by the authorities as the new capital.
Investment in Kazakhstan totals $2 billion so far.
